title: Age gate leaves an orphan modal backdrop that swallows every click
description:
Found incidentally while smoke-testing MPI-376 in the browser surface, NOT a masking bug. SYMPTOM: accepting the 18+ adult-content gate (CONTINUE) removes the modal's CONTENT but leaves the backdrop element behind. Measured in the live DOM immediately after dismissal:
children: 0, rect: 1280x688 (full viewport), z-index: 10009, pointer-events: auto Because it is full-viewport with pointer-events auto at a very high z-index, it intercepts EVERY click on the landing page. Playwright reported '
intercepts pointer events' and retried until timeout on a plain project-tile click. A human would see a landing page where nothing is clickable. Removing the node by hand restored normal interaction, which confirms the backdrop is the sole cause. REPRO (browser, fresh profile so the gate actually shows): 1. Serve the app and open http://127.0.0.1:3000/ in a profile that has never accepted the gate. 2. Click CONTINUE on 'Adult content - 18+ only'. 3. Try to click a recent-project tile. Nothing happens. 4. document.querySelectorAll('.mpi-modal-backdrop') returns one childless full-viewport node. UNKNOWN AND MUST BE CHECKED FIRST: whether Electron leaks the same node. The gate is accepted once per install, so on a normal desktop run it may never be seen again after first launch - which would make this a first-run-only defect there, or browser-only if the desktop path differs. Check the desktop first-run before deciding severity; a first-run dead landing page in the ship target is serious, a dev-browser-only annoyance is not. ROOT CAUSE IS NOT DIAGNOSED YET. Do not patch it by deleting stray backdrops on a timer or on route change - that is exactly the symptom-patch the root-cause rule forbids. Find the teardown path that removes the modal body without removing its backdrop. Likely home is the shell overlay/modal service (docs/shell.md covers Overlays) or whichever component mounts the age gate; check whether the gate dismisses itself directly instead of going through the overlay manager's teardown, which would explain a half-removal. SWEEP: if the gate bypasses the shared teardown, every other consumer of that modal path is suspect too - grep them and classify rather than fixing the gate alone.
acceptance: Root cause named: WHICH teardown path removes the modal content but not the backdrop, and why
Electron first-run checked explicitly - state whether the desktop target leaks the same node or not, with evidence
After dismissing the gate, document.querySelectorAll('.mpi-modal-backdrop').length is 0 and the landing page is fully clickable
Fixed at the teardown, NOT by sweeping up stray backdrops on a timer, route change or interval
Every other consumer of that modal/overlay teardown path is grepped and classified - a gate-only fix on a shared primitive is a false done
If the backdrop belongs to a shared overlay service, its teardown contract is recorded in docs/shell.md
